components.name: Primary Action Button
components.description: Filled cobalt pill with a solid/checkmark-style icon; the confirming action in any button pair.

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:8px 14px; border-radius:9999px; border:none; font-size:13px; font-weight:600; color:#fff; background:#3a5fe0; cursor:pointer; transition:background 0.15s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#3151c7; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background:#2944ad; transform:scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #3a5fe0; outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Secondary Action Button
components.description: Outline pill with a play/pause-style icon; the neutral action in any button pair.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-secondary"><svg width="11" height="11" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M6 4l14 8-14 8V4z" fill="currentColor"/></svg>시작</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:8px 14px; border-radius:9999px; border:1px solid rgba(20,21,26,0.08); font-size:13px; font-weight:600; color:#14151a; background:transparent; cursor:pointer; transition:background 0.15s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background:color-mix(in srgb, white 84%, transparent); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform:scale(0.97); }

components.name: Glass Card (NoteCardFrame)
components.description: Compact glass card for a non-active note: type/tag/status row, title, subtitle, optional thin progress bar, action row.

components.description: The single full-width glass widget for whichever note currently holds the timer: ring dial + tabular countdown, phase dot+label, title/subtitle, action row.

components.name: Type/Status Dot+Label
components.description: The dot-plus-neutral-label pattern shared by TypeBadge, StatusTag, TagDot — color never carries meaning alone.

components.name: Field Input (TimeInput/DurationInput)
components.description: Flat-filled nested control (not glass) used for time/duration/text entry inside a sheet; inset colored ring on focus, no border-color swap.

components.description: Done/failed/skipped summary row: solid-fill status-color circle with a white SVG glyph (check/minus/chevron), never raw text characters, guaranteeing contrast on any status color.

narrative.overview: PomodoroTimer's popup is a small frosted-glass instrument panel: one glass hero widget states what's running right now, and everything else recedes into a compressed, scannable list of glass cards. The world is deliberately quiet — a single graphite/white surface language, one cobalt accent, and a continuous (never stepped) color language for urgency — because the product's job is a 1-second glance while working, not a destination to linger in. Nothing here shouts; the hero widget is the only thing allowed to be large, and it earns that size by being the one note currently holding the timer. Two disciplines were inherited from the direction contract's near-miss challenger and are now load-bearing: state is never color-only (every dot pairs with a neutral-text label), and action buttons are differentiated by shape as well as color (filled pill for the confirming action, outlined pill for the secondary one). Depth comes entirely from translucency and soft, deeply-blurred shadows, never from hard offsets or borders alone — this is a frosted-glass world, and its blur is structural, not decorative.
keyCharacteristics: One cobalt accent (#3a5fe0), used sparingly against a graphite/white neutral field
A single hero widget per screen state; everything else is a compact card
Continuous, color-mix–driven ring color rather than discrete status colors
State is always dot + neutral-text label, never color alone
Primary vs. secondary actions differ in shape (filled pill vs. outline pill), not just color

rules.name: The Dot-Plus-Label Rule
rules.body: Every semantic state (note type, tag, status) is shown as a small color dot beside a neutral-colored text label. Color alone never carries meaning — the dot is the color channel, the label is the reading channel, and they always travel together.

rules.name: The Continuous Urgency Rule
rules.body: The timer ring's color is not a palette of discrete steps; it is color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-urgent) {urgency%}, var(--color-accent)), where urgency is a cubic ease of remaining-time progress. The ring visibly warms as time runs out rather than jumping between fixed colors — except during a break phase, where it holds flat at Break Green because there is nothing to hurry.

rules.name: The Tabular Timer Rule
rules.body: Any digit display representing a live countdown or duration uses tabular-nums. A ticking timer must never cause surrounding layout to jitter.

rules.name: The Inline Blur Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter is applied via an inline style object (glassBlur in src/utils/colorUtils.ts), never as a plain CSS class rule. This project's Tailwind v4 / Lightning CSS build silently strips an unprefixed backdrop-filter declaration when written in global.css, keeping only the -webkit- prefix (which alone does not render blur in this Chromium build). .glass-surface therefore only owns background; any new glass surface must pair className="glass-surface ..." with style={{ ...glassBlur, ... }} or it silently renders flat and non-blurred, double-exposing whatever is stacked behind it.

rules.name: The Squircle-Or-Pill Rule
rules.body: A surface is either a large rounded rectangle (24px or 20px) or a fully-rounded pill/circle. There is no intermediate corner radius used for a whole container — 10-14px radii are reserved for nested form controls inside a 20px+ parent, never for a top-level card.

rules.name: The Shape-Not-Just-Color Rule
rules.body: Primary and secondary actions are never distinguished by color alone: primary is always filled + a "commit" icon shape, secondary is always outlined + a "start/neutral" icon shape. A confirming action must be visually assignable even in grayscale.

dos: Do pair every color-carrying dot with a neutral-text label (Dot-Plus-Label Rule).
Do apply backdrop-filter via the glassBlur inline-style object alongside .glass-surface, never as a plain CSS class declaration (Inline Blur Rule).
Do drive the timer ring's color through the continuous ringColorFor() color-mix rather than a stepped palette, holding it flat only for the break phase.
Do keep the hero widget singular — one active note gets the large glass treatment; every other note in view stays a compact card.
Do use tabular-nums on any live-updating countdown or duration digit.
donts: Don't introduce a flat, opaque (non-glass) container for any card/dialog/sheet surface — glass tint + blur + hairline border is this system's only container treatment.
Don't differentiate primary/secondary actions by color alone — shape (filled pill vs. outline pill) and icon style must differ too.
Don't use a hard-offset, non-blurred shadow anywhere in this world; all shadows here are large, soft, and negatively-offset (ambient), matching the Shadow Vocabulary above.

Don't raise a card's radius above 20px or below it for a top-level container — 24px is reserved for the hero/sheet; 20px is the card/dialog standard; nothing top-level sits between them or below them.
